thread:
Sam K: Heads-up — I'm taking my laptop offline at 20:00 PT for a family call. Handing primary to Maya. Leaving notes below, please ack if you see gaps.
Maya R: ack — I'll be primary from 20:00–04:00 PT. Sam, anything sticky right now?
Sam K: nothing active. Two things to watch: 1) EU batch jobs still flaky after the rolling config change earlier (see last incident thread), 2) a warm node in dedicated pool 3a has ~15% CPU creep.
Maya R: noted. I'll kick off a quick health sweep when I take over. Anyone on secondary tonight?
Jess L: I'm secondary for 20:00–00:00 PT, then Oliver takes over.
Oliver P: yep, I'm on 00:00–08:00 PT. I'll be reachable via phone.
Nina C: adding runbook links here: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/ONCALL-RUNBOOK (primary incident play), https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/POOL-HEALTH (pool ops).
Carlos G: +1. For paging: follow the paging matrix in the runbook — SEV1: primary -> 5m -> secondary -> 10m -> oncall-lead (@Sam K or @Maya R). SEV2: primary -> 10m -> secondary. SEV3: slack-only unless customer escalates.
Sam K: copying matrix here for quick reference: 
```
Paging matrix (quick):
- SEV1: page primary (phone + push). If no ack in 5m, page secondary. If still no ack in 10m, escalate to oncall-lead and notify eng-sre.
- SEV2: page primary (push). No ack in 10m -> page secondary. Escalate to lead if customer impact or >30m.
- SEV3: slack notification, monitor, open ticket if persistent.
- Region-specific: EU business hours -> include EU-duty in first escalation for regional incidents.
```
Maya R: thanks — small tweak: for Dedicated pool OOMs we page infra-team after secondary if it's obviously hardware. Add that to the OOM appendix.
Jess L: noted. Also, if incident-bot autofires SEV1 between 20:00–22:00 PT, treat as urgent and assume primary is on-call (don't wait around). We had a missed page before.
incident-bot: [ALERT] automated SEV1 detected for job: eu-batch-worker. Triggered 3xx error spikes. Pager rule: immediate page to primary.
Maya R: seeing the bot alert. I'm running quick checks: 
```
curl -s https://infra-api.internal/pool/3a/health | jq .
# look for "oom": true or cpu > 85
```
Maya R: pool 3a shows CPU ramp to 78%, no OOMs. EU batch job errors correlated with last config rollout id 2026-03-12T03:00Z — rollback candidate.
Oliver P: if rollback needed, checklist: 1) tag current model/version, 2) execute rollback via /ops/deploy pipeline, 3) monitor for 15m, 4) notify customers if degraded. Runbook link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/ROLLBACK-CHECKLIST
Nina C: quick reminder about customer-impact triage: use the incident form (internal) and set "customer_impact": high/medium/low. If high, page support lead immediately even for SEV2.
Carlos G: phone numbers — primary paging uses PagerDuty; fallback dial chain: +1-415-555-0101 (primary oncall) -> +1-415-555-0102 (secondary) -> +1-415-555-0103 (oncall lead).
Sam K: minute-by-minute handoff notes: 
- 19:58: cross-check alerts, confirm PD escalation window cleared.
- 19:59: update #oncall-meta sticky with primary/secondary and contact numbers.
- 20:00: change status in runbook dashboard to Maya (primary).
Maya R: done — status set and PD escalations confirmed. I ran the health curl above and opened a quick ticket for batch failures. Ticket ID: OPS-5421.
Jess L: acked through 21:30 — ping me if it goes to SEV1 again.
Oliver P: I'll keep my phone on and monitor logs after midnight.
Sam K: couple of fallback options if paging fails: 
- If PD unresponsive, escalate in slack to #eng-sre and call the fallback chain above.
- If primary machine unreachable (VPN issues), use web console from pagerduty or ask support to create an emergency jump host.
Maya R: small operational note — for any rollback, coordinate with product ops (they own customer comms). I can loop them in if we pull the trigger.
incident-bot: [INFO] scheduled job: nightly-eu-maintenance starting 23:00 PT. This may increase noise. Please set filters if needed.
Nina C: filter tip: in runbook dashboard -> Filters -> suppress "maintenance:info" for 23:00–00:30 PT. But don't suppress SEV or error rates.
Carlos G: leaving a quick escalation decision tree snippet for whoever is primary: 
1) Identify impact (customer-facing? all regions? number of customers).
2) If customer-facing and >5% error rate -> SEV1. Page immediately.
3) If internal batch jobs failing only -> SEV2 unless it impacts downstream product features.
4) If unsure -> page secondary and start triage, better to over-notify.
Maya R: thanks, will follow. One last item: gap coverage 02:00–03:00 PT — no dedicated secondary on rotation (holiday shifts). Oliver, can you cover emergency pages in that window?
Oliver P: can do 02:00–03:00 PT emergency cover. I'll be on call phone in that hour.
Sam K: perfect. Everyone: final ack please so I can close the handoff.
Maya R: ack — thanks Sam.
Jess L: ack.
Oliver P: ack.
Nina C: ack.
Carlos G: ack.
Sam K: leaving now — thanks team, ping if anything spikes. :wave:
Maya R: thanks — taking over. I'll post a short status update at 21:00 PT.
